# Changes in version 1.3.1.9000 (2026-10-05)

**This version requires R \>=4.5.0**

## Breaking changes

The following S3 methods (deprecated in v1.3.1) have been removed
(#1694):

- `as.data.frame.RLum.Data.*` (use `as.data.frame()` instead)
- `as.list.RLum.*` (use `as.list()` instead)
- `as.matrix.RLum.Data.*` (use `as.matrix()` instead)
- `dim.RLum.Data.*` (use `dim()` instead)
- `hist.RLum.*` (use `hist()` instead)
- `length.RLum.*`, `length.Risoe.BINfileData`, `length_RLum` (use
  `length()` instead)
- `merge_RLum.*` (use `merge_RLum()` instead)
- `names.RLum.*`, `names.Risoe.BINfileData`, `names_RLum` (use `names()`
  instead)
- `plot.RLum.*` (use `plot_RLum()` instead)
- `summary.RLum.*` (use `summary()` instead)

The following functions are no longer exported, but their functionality
can be accessed via the `plot_RLum()` generic (#1775):

- `plot_RLum.Analysis()`
- `plot_RLum.Data.Curve()`
- `plot_RLum.Data.Image()`
- `plot_RLum.Data.Spectrum()`
- `plot_RLum.Results()`

The following functions are no longer exported, but their functionality
can be accessed via the new `bin_RLum()` generic (#1782):

- `bin()`
- `bin.RLum.Data.Curve()`
- `bin.RLum.Data.Spectrum()`
- `bin_RLum.Data()`

## New functions

## Bugfixes and changes

### `analyse_IRSAR.RF()`

- Swap fitting using `nls()` and the `port` algorithm with
  `minpack.lm::nlsLM()` along with some code tunings. This should have
  no user-visible effects other than better and more reliable fitting in
  the case where `method = "FIT"` was chosen (#1748).

### `analyse_SAR.CWOSL()`

- The `plot_onePage` argument now defaults to `TRUE` as this turned out
  to be a more meaningful default value than `FALSE`.

### `bin_RLum()`

- The function no longer throws an error when applied to an empty
  `RLum.Data.Spectrum` object, but returns the object itself. This
  uniforms the behaviour to the one used when handling `RLum.Data.Curve`
  objects.

### `fit_DoseResponseCurve()`

- The new `fit.IndexRegPoints` replaces both `fit.NumberRegPoints` and
  `fit.NumberRegPointsReal`. This accepts the indices of the
  regeneration points to be used in fitting, thus providing a quick way
  to check for the impact of additional regeneration points. The older
  arguments will raise a deprecation warning and will be ignored
  (#1762).

### `get_RLum()`

- When applied to a list with a `class` argument matching none of the
  list elements, the `class` filter was silently ignored. The filter is
  now always applied, so such a call returns an empty list instead of
  the unfiltered contents (#1778).

### `merge_RLum()`

- The function no longer crashes when attempting to merge an empty
  `RLum.Data.Spectrum` object (#1771).

- The function is now implemented as an S4 generic that allows automatic
  dispatch according to the type of elements being merged. This means
  that external packages can now fully overload it for their own classes
  (#1769).

- Merging of more than two `RLum.Data.Spectrum` objects produced an
  incorrect result when `merge.method` was one of `-`, `*` or `/`
  (#1773).

### `plot_DoseResponseCurve()`

- The presence of a repeated zero-dose point caused the plot not to
  print the last dose point in `mode = "alternate"`. This was a
  regression partially introduced in v1.0.0 (#1762).

- Repeated regenerated points were plotted twice: once as a normal dose
  (full circle), then as a repeated dose (triangle). Also repeated
  zero-dose points were overplotted with two different symbols. Now each
  point appears only once in the plot: only the first zero-dose point is
  plotted as a reg 0 point (empty circle if `mode == "interpolation"`),
  repeated points (zero-dose or not) are plotted only as a repeated
  point (triangle), while the rest are considered regenerated dose
  points (#1766).

### `plot_RLum()`

- The function is now implemented as an S4 generic that allows automatic
  dispatch according to the type of elements being plotted. This means
  that external packages can now fully overload it for their own classes
  (#1775).

### `plot_RLum.Analysis()`

- Using the `sub_title` graphical parameter (accepted via …) will raise
  a deprecation warning and be ignored; the more standard `sub`
  parameter should be used instead. As a consequence, the `subset`
  argument must be spelled out in full and can no longer be abbreviated
  to `sub` or anything else (#1776).

### `plot_RLum.Data.Spectrum()`

- The function could not plot objects containing only integer counts in
  the spectrum due to overly-stringent validation (#1780).

### `read_BIN2R()`

- The `pattern` argument is now validated to be a single string to avoid
  the `dir()` behaviour of silently ignoring all but the first pattern
  (#1751).

- The `pattern` argument is no longer ignored when `file` contains more
  than one input files or directories (#1753).

- The function could get trapped in an infinite loop if any records
  declares to have size 0 (#1759).

- If `position` was specified but not all the provided positions were
  present in the file, then all curves were returned instead of only
  those with matching positions. Now `position` is always respected,
  even when no positions match, in which case an empty object is
  returned (#1784; thanks to Annette Kadereit for reporting).

### `read_XSYG2R()`

- The `pattern` argument is now validated to be a single string to avoid
  the `dir()` behaviour of silently ignoring all but the first pattern
  (#1751).

- The `pattern` argument is no longer ignored when `file` contains more
  than one input files or directories (#1753).
